source_evidence: Most smart investors put enough money in savings to cover an emergency, like sudden unemployment.
answer: An emergency fund is money set aside in savings to help cover an unexpected event, such as sudden unemployment. The source notes that some people keep up to six months of their income in savings. Savings can be kept in places that allow access to money when needed, but this security and availability come with a tradeoff: savings earn a low interest rate, which may not keep up with inflation.
